author: EmuCore - Hub
title: DuckStation documents PlayStation Mouse support across regional game entries
summary: A broad GameDB audit adds the mouse to compatible serials and disables automatic analog mode for titles where analog sticks are nonfunctional, improving controller choices without a core-input guess.
heroAlt: Source evidence from DuckStation pull request #3662: GameDB: Add mouse support for compatible games

sourceLabels.duckstation-pr-3662: GameDB: Add mouse support for compatible games

blocks.text: Peripheral support is a property of the disc, not only the emulator

DuckStation can emulate a PlayStation Mouse, but the frontend needs to know which games were designed to accept it. Without compatibility data, users may never be offered the device or may attach it blindly to software that expects a pad. Pull request #3662 audits GameDB serials and records PlayStationMouse in supportedControllers, keeping the decision attached to the exact game and region.
Regional families receive the same peripheral declaration

The diff covers many SLES, SLPS, SLUS, and SCUS records, including multi-disc and regional variants. Some entries list both AnalogController and PlayStationMouse because the game legitimately supports more than one device. This is not a global default and does not force mouse input at runtime; it gives controller selection and automatic configuration accurate options for each known serial.
DisableAutoAnalogMode handles titles whose sticks do nothing

The same audit adds DisableAutoAnalogMode to specific records where analog sticks are ineffective. That prevents DuckStation from automatically choosing a mode that appears modern but leaves the game unresponsive. Mouse support and analog-mode policy are related only through the title's input capabilities: one adds a valid device, while the other stops an invalid automatic assumption.
Every serial needs an input-path check, not just database validation

For representative entries, connect the emulated mouse, verify motion and buttons in menus and gameplay, and confirm pad input still works where AnalogController remains listed. Test regional variants and every disc in a set. Entries with DisableAutoAnalogMode should boot into a responsive default yet allow manual changes where supported. A database linter can catch malformed lists, but only game tests can catch a serial that was classified from an incorrect manual or regional assumption.
The audit makes the controller picker evidence-based: offer a PlayStation Mouse where the disc supports it and avoid analog defaults where the game ignores them.
